title: Beef with Rice and Vegetables in Tomato Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of lean beef, boiled rice and a mix of vegetables – carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens (spinach, kale). All ingredients are simmered in a flavorful tomato‑based sauce, making the meal nutritious and balanced.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is a rich source of heme iron, which is better absorbed when paired with vitamin C from tomatoes.
Rice provides quick‑release carbohydrates; whole‑grain varieties add dietary fiber.
Broccoli contains sulforaphane, a compound with anti‑inflammatory properties.
Dark‑green leafy greens are high in vitamin K, essential for blood clotting.
Tomato sauce made from ripe tomatoes is abundant in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: Beef protein aids muscle growth and repair, especially when combined with the carbs from rice.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Vitamin C from tomatoes and beta‑carotene from carrots enhance the body’s defense mechanisms.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Calcium and vitamin K from leafy greens contribute to bone mineralization.

items.title: Digestive health
items.content: Fiber from broccoli, carrots and greens promotes healthy intestinal motility.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene and sulforaphane protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Excess red meat intake
items.content: Consuming large amounts of beef may increase cardiovascular risk; moderation is advised.

items.title: Sodium in the sauce
items.content: Tomato sauce often contains added salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Vegetable allergies
items.content: Rarely, individuals may react to broccoli or leafy greens.

items.title: Gluten in the sauce
items.content: If the sauce is thickened with wheat flour, the dish is not suitable for a gluten‑free diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sear beef cubes until browned, then add cooked rice, sliced carrots, broccoli florets and greens. Simmer in tomato sauce for 10‑15 minutes. Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs or grated Parmesan.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the dish to room temperature, then place in an airtight container. Store in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat thoroughly to a rolling boil before serving.
